title: Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills
content:
## 1.4 Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills

### 1.4.1 The fit to be demonstrated: a dual profile for a dual project

The assessment under this sub-criterion turns on a single question: does the experienced researcher already possess the professional experience, competences and skills that make the FIELDWISE research programme achievable in her hands, and are they appropriate — not merely adjacent — to what the project actually requires? FIELDWISE is, by construction, a dual undertaking. Its scientific spine runs from a physiologically grounded definition of processing-tomato water stress, through a proximal-hyperspectral-to-Sentinel bridge, to prospective, uncertainty-aware, transferability-tested prediction and field-level decision value. Answering it therefore demands one person who can both define and measure crop water-stress physiology in the field and reason about scalable geospatial prediction. The applicant, Dr. Rositsa Cholakova (who published before 2020 under the name Rositsa Cholakova-Bimbalova, a change first noted here so that her earlier record attaches unambiguously to the same person), holds exactly this dual profile: a mature, evidenced foundation in plant physiology, agronomy and water-stress experimentation, joined to a deliberate and documented trajectory into Earth observation, GIS and agricultural data science. The remainder of this sub-section shows that the foundation is directly appropriate to the project's physiological and agronomic core, that the geospatial trajectory is real and load-bearing rather than asserted, and — in the honest register the whole proposal adopts — where the profile is still developing and how the fellowship's training (detailed in §1.3, not repeated here) closes precisely that residual gap.

### 1.4.2 The disciplinary foundation: plant physiology, agronomy and water-stress experimentation

The researcher's core professional experience is in the exact discipline FIELDWISE places at the root of its methodology. She holds a doctorate in Plant Physiology, awarded in 2020 by Agricultural University – Plovdiv (Faculty of Agronomy, Department of Plant Physiology and Biochemistry; doctoral programme Plant Physiology, professional field Agronomy, EQF level 8, 291 ECTS), following doctoral studies from 2014 to 2020 supervised by Prof. Dr. Andon Vassilev. Her doctoral research addressed the response of a field crop to abiotic (low-temperature) stress and the effectiveness of a subsequent agronomic intervention — the same class of problem, crop-stress physiology under an environmental constraint plus a management response, that FIELDWISE tackles for water stress in processing tomato. She then served as Assistant Professor in Plant Physiology and Plant Stress Physiology at Agricultural University, Plovdiv (2015–2020), and is currently Chief Assistant Professor and plant physiology researcher at Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute (from October 2024), where the vegetable-crop and abiotic-stress remit sits squarely inside the FIELDWISE problem space.

This foundation is appropriate to the project in the strict sense the criterion requires, because it supplies precisely the competences the project depends upon and that its host's remote-sensing group does not itself hold: plant physiology, horticultural crop science, plant protection and agronomy, water-stress experimentation, physiological phenotyping, hyperspectral field measurements and the biological interpretation of Earth-observation signals. These are not generic strengths; they are the specific inputs to O1 (defining a physiologically meaningful stress target rather than a spectral proxy) and to the physiological early-warning hypothesis on which the project's novelty rests. The relevance is further reinforced by a live, funded thread in the researcher's own portfolio: she works on abiotic stress — drought and salinity — in *Solanum lycopersicum* (the FIELDWISE crop and one of the FIELDWISE stresses) within a currently running institutional project, and participates in a further tomato multi-stress-tolerance action. Her professional experience is therefore not merely compatible with the science of FIELDWISE; it is continuous with it.

### 1.4.3 The Earth-observation and geospatial trajectory: real, evidenced, and honestly scoped

FIELDWISE's second half — scalable prediction from hyperspectral and Sentinel data, with transferability and decision value — requires geospatial and data-science competence, and the proposal is deliberately candid about the nature and current maturity of the researcher's evidence here. Her move into Earth observation, GIS and agricultural data science is documented not principally through publications but through concrete professional activity, which is the appropriate and honest way to evidence an emerging competence. Specifically: she was a Short-Term Scientific Mission awardee under COST Action CA22136 PANGEOS, hosted at Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem in Hungary in 2025 — the very institution that supplies the FIELDWISE source-domain dataset — giving her direct, recent working contact with the project's data environment; she has held Erasmus+ staff-mobility grants at Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem and at the University of Novi Sad (2025–2026) and an earlier Erasmus master's mobility internship at the host itself, Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest; she holds a UAV pilot licence (A1/A3, Civil Aviation Administration of Bulgaria), which is directly pertinent to proximal and airborne data acquisition; and she is a member of three relevant COST Actions (CA22136 PANGEOS, CA22149 AI4Insect and CA22141 REcrop). Her recent publications include a small number that touch remote sensing (from 2025, as a middle author), so the proposal states plainly that the Earth-observation half of the profile rests on these missions, mobilities and the UAV licence — and on demonstrated prototyping — rather than on a deep independent publication record. This honest scoping is itself a quality signal, and it is consistent with the evidential discipline the whole proposal maintains.

The single most concrete piece of evidence that the researcher can operate across the physiology/geospatial divide is that she has already built a working artefact that does so. She has initiated DrR – Digital Agronomist, a desktop research prototype (and her background intellectual property) that integrates soil-sensor information, field meteorological observations and Sentinel-2 data in a common digital environment. This prototype is the preliminary development she brings into the host as part of the two-way transfer of knowledge, and it is the technical seed from which the project's operational endpoint grows. That she conceived and built it demonstrates, more persuasively than any credential, that the interdisciplinary integration FIELDWISE demands is within her existing capability rather than a hoped-for outcome.

### 1.4.4 Teaching, communication and applied professional experience

Beyond research, the researcher brings substantial and directly transferable professional experience. She taught for five years at Agricultural University, Plovdiv (2015–2020), where her duties included syllabus design, lecturing and examining in both Bulgarian and English (including for Erasmus students) and the supervision of student research projects and Bachelor's theses; she also acted as a specialist consultant to farmers on physiological monitoring and integrated plant protection. This is a mature teaching and science-communication competence, and it is appropriate to FIELDWISE on two counts: it underpins the teaching and public-engagement commitments the project makes to the host (feeding research results back into education), and its farmer-facing, advisory dimension is exactly the sensibility the project's operational-transfer and decision-value strand requires when it engages commercial growers. Consistent with the honest framing used throughout, this teaching experience is presented as an existing strength to be transferred into a new discipline, a new institution and a new language of instruction — and stepped up from Bachelor's to Master's and doctoral supervision — rather than as a competence still to be acquired. Her applied, non-academic professional experience is also pertinent: she has worked as an Agricultural Market Analyst (Kleffmann Group Bulgaria) and, more recently, as a Data Analyst at KPMG Global Hungary, the latter adding practical data-analysis exposure that complements the project's data-science demands and the inter-sectoral orientation of her intended career path.

### 1.4.5 Breadth, currency and mobility of the track record

The researcher's competence base is broad and actively current rather than static. In addition to her doctorate she holds an MSc and BSc in Plant Protection and is completing a second master's in Environmental Engineering (2025–2026), evidencing a sustained, self-directed widening of her competences toward the environmental-modelling and data-analytic demands of FIELDWISE. Her project experience spans institutional and national instruments in her home environment — including a running abiotic-stress project on the FIELDWISE crop and a national project on satellite and UAV monitoring of vegetable crops for precision agriculture, undertaken with the Space Research and Technology Institute of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences — as well as participation in a Horizon Europe MSCA Staff Exchange action on tomato multi-stress tolerance. This portfolio shows both thematic continuity with FIELDWISE and growing engagement with the EU research ecosystem, and it is reinforced by a genuinely international mobility record (doctoral and staff mobilities across Hungary, Serbia and beyond). The breadth is appropriate rather than diffuse: every strand — crop-stress physiology, precision-agriculture remote sensing, environmental engineering, data analysis, UAV operation — converges on one of the competences FIELDWISE integrates.

### 1.4.6 Appropriateness overall, honest gaps, and the fit to the fellowship

Taken together, the researcher's professional experience is of high quality and closely appropriate to the proposed research: she brings the physiological, agronomic and experimental core of the project as evidenced, mature competence; she brings a real and documented — if still developing — geospatial and data-science trajectory, anchored by a working cross-domain prototype; and she brings teaching, communication and applied-analytic experience that maps onto the project's training and operational commitments. The proposal does not overstate this fit. It states openly that her deepest publication record lies on the physiological side, that the Earth-observation side currently rests on missions, mobilities, the UAV licence and prototyping, and that a defined residual competence gap remains — in Bayesian and spatio-temporal modelling, sensor transfer, uncertainty quantification, domain adaptation and decision-oriented evaluation. This gap is not a weakness concealed but the precise object of the fellowship's scientific and methodological training set out in §1.3, and it is what makes FIELDWISE a genuine developmental opportunity rather than a mere continuation of existing work. The intended progression the profile supports — from Plant Physiologist/Agronomist, to Earth-observation/geospatial crop scientist, to an independent researcher in transferable agricultural intelligence — is realistic precisely because the applicant already stands at the interface of the two domains the project unites. This directly serves the call's expected outcome that a fellow acquire an increased set of research and transferable skills leading to improved employability within academia and beyond.

Two further points bear on appropriateness and are disclosed rather than glossed. First, the researcher took a full-time parenting career break (July 2021 to May 2024, in Budapest); this is declared in Part A, does not count against the research-experience eligibility ceiling, and does not detract from the currency of her competences, which her 2024–2026 positions, second master's, STSM, mobilities and running projects all evidence as active. Second, FIELDWISE is a considered resubmission: the applicant and the same host previously prepared and submitted the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal PLANTDIGISENSE, which scored 70.40% against a 70.00 threshold. This is material to the assessment of her professional readiness because it evidences a tested applicant–host relationship and a proposal already judged of fundable quality, which the present objective architecture is designed to strengthen rather than merely repair. Where individual profile details remain to be finalised for the Part B-2 CV (for example, any record of invited talks has not yet been supplied and is not asserted here, and the exact official title of the doctoral thesis is rendered from its published abstract pending the original), these are declared open rather than filled speculatively — consistent with the evidential standard the evaluator can expect the researcher herself to bring to the work.

claim_statuses.claim_summary: The applicant is Dr. Rositsa Cholakova, plant physiologist, Chief Assistant Professor at Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute, publishing before 2020 as Rositsa Cholakova-Bimbalova.
PhD in Plant Physiology awarded 2020 by Agricultural University – Plovdiv (EQF 8, 291 ECTS; doctoral studies 2014–2020; supervisor Prof. Dr. Andon Vassilev).

The doctoral thesis concerns a field crop's response to low-temperature (abiotic) stress and a subsequent foliar-fertilisation response; the English title is an inferred rendering of the Bulgarian original.
Current position: Chief Assistant Professor / plant physiology researcher at MVCRI, Agricultural Academy, Plovdiv, from 2024-10-15.

Prior positions include Assistant Professor in Plant Physiology and Plant Stress Physiology (AU Plovdiv 2015–2020), Data Analyst at KPMG Global Hungary (2024), and Agricultural Market Analyst at Kleffmann Group Bulgaria (2013).

Five years of university teaching at AU Plovdiv (2015–2020): syllabus design, lecturing and examining in Bulgarian and English incl. Erasmus students, Bachelor's-thesis supervision, farmer advisory on physiological monitoring and integrated plant protection.

Nine publications, two DOI-bearing; only three touch remote sensing (2025+, middle author); the EO half of the profile rests on the STSM, Erasmus mobilities, the UAV licence and prototyping rather than on publications.

STSM awardee under COST Action CA22136 PANGEOS hosted at MATE (2025); Erasmus+ staff mobilities at MATE and University of Novi Sad (2025–2026); earlier Erasmus master's internship at ELTE; UAV pilot licence A1/A3; member of COST Actions CA22136, CA22149, CA22141.

Running/near-term projects include ZEMDKT 17 (drought and salinity in Solanum lycopersicum), KP-06-COST/2 (satellite/UAV vegetable-crop monitoring with the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences' Space Research and Technology Institute), and MSCA-SE SolGenSys (tomato multi-stress tolerance).
Holds MSc and BSc in Plant Protection and is completing a second MSc in Environmental Engineering (2025–2026).

The researcher initiated DrR – Digital Agronomist, a desktop research prototype (her background IP) integrating soil-sensor, field-meteorological and Sentinel-2 data, brought in as part of the fellow-to-host transfer.

The researcher brings plant physiology, horticultural crop science, plant protection/agronomy, water-stress experimentation, physiological phenotyping, hyperspectral field measurements and biological interpretation of EO as her existing competences.
Intended career progression: Plant Physiologist/Agronomist → EO/Geospatial Crop Scientist → independent researcher in transferable agricultural intelligence.
A residual competence gap in Bayesian modelling, spatio-temporal AI, sensor transfer, uncertainty, domain adaptation and decision evaluation remains and is the object of the fellowship's training.
A full-time parenting career break (2021-07-25 to 2024-05-31, Budapest) is declared in Part A and does not count against the research-experience ceiling.
FIELDWISE is a resubmission: the same applicant and host previously submitted PLANTDIGISENSE (HORIZON-MSCA-2025-PF), which scored 70.40% against a 70.00 threshold.
The profile-plus-fellowship serves the call's expected outcome of an increased set of research and transferable skills leading to improved employability within and beyond academia (EO-01).
The host is Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) and the fellowship's training closes the researcher's residual gap (context established in §1.3).
Any record of invited talks has not been supplied and is not asserted in the profile.
